messages:
Anna (CS): Quick ask — prepping a short, customer-facing 'lite rollout' runbook for new accounts (esp mid-market) that includes checks for caching, batching, and streaming fallbacks. Need something we can send to customers and also use internally for handoffs. Keep it action-oriented and short.

Mike (SRE): +1. I can add the quick telemetry queries and a tiny ops checklist. Want this to be < 1 page for customers.

Sophia (PM): Suggest 3 sections: readiness checklist, live troubleshooting knobs, and escalation + feedback loop. Customers like examples they can paste.

Anna (CS): Exactly. Also include a tiny sample config and an email template to capture early feedback / renewal risk signal.

Raj (Customer): From the customer side — we want one thing to tweak first if latency spikes. Usually we flip caching or reduce batch size.

Mike (SRE): Short ops checklist (for us/internal):
- Verify model pinned & version match
- Confirm prefix cache warms (sample query below)
- Observe 95th percentile latency and token throughput for first 10m of live traffic
- If latency > target, enable KV-prefill and reduce target_batch_size by 30%

ops-bot: Deployment: customer/nimbus-ai/production v2026.03 rolled to 3 nodes at 3612345700 UTC :rocket:

Anna (CS): Customer-facing one-pager (single Slack/email block they can copy):
"""
Lite Rollout Quick Guide — (paste into your onboarding doc)
1) Readiness (5 minutes)
  - Confirm model & region: model=redwood-boost-1, region=us-west-2
  - Prefill: enable prefix cache with TTL=600s for known welcome prompts
  - Batching: start with target_batch_size=16, max_latency_ms=120
2) Fast recovery knobs (use if latency or errors spike)
  - Toggle: disable streaming to fall back to non-streaming short responses
  - Cache: increase cache TTL to 1200s for low-variance prompts
  - Batch: reduce target_batch_size to 8 and set max_latency_ms=80
3) Telemetry to watch (first 30m)
  - 95th_latency_by_route > 200ms = action threshold
  - cache_hit_rate < 60% => revisit prefill items
4) Safety valve: if errors > 1% for 5m, set fallback_model=redwood-lite-v1 and notify support@redwood.com
5) Feedback: send this short pulse at 24h: "How are the responses matching expectations? Any timeouts or rate limits?"
"""

Sophia (PM): Love it. Add a tiny sample JSON snippet for the SDK config so customers can paste:
```json
{"model":"redwood-boost-1","prefill_cache":{"enabled":true,"ttl_seconds":600},"batching":{"target_batch_size":16,"max_latency_ms":120},"streaming":true}
```

Anna (CS): And a 1-paragraph customer email template for feedback + renewal signal capture:
"""
Hi Raj —
Congrats on going live! Quick favor: could you share any observations after 24 hours about latency, unexpected errors, or quality? If you hit timeouts, try turning off streaming briefly and toggle cache TTL to 1200s.
If things look smooth, tell us what workloads you expect next month (peak users/day) — this helps us recommend a dedicated pool early and avoid contention that often drives renewal concerns.
Thanks,
Anna — Customer Success (Redwood)
"""

Mike (SRE): PromQL-ish queries to include for internal handoffs:
- rate(redwood_infer_requests_total[5m]) by (route)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_infer_response_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- sum(rate(redwood_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_cache_lookup_total[5m]))

Anna (CS): Escalation matrix (customer-facing short bullets):
- Tier 1: CS rep (Anna) — initial triage and config suggestions
- Tier 2: SRE on-call (Mike) — if 95p latency > target after tweaks or errors persist > 5m
- Tier 3: Dedicated infra lead (onboarded infra pager) — for capacity or model fallback decisions

Raj (Customer): Super helpful. For our team, could you also add a one-line explanation: when to prefer increasing cache TTL vs adding prefill items?

Anna (CS): One-liner we can give customers: "Increase cache TTL when your prompts are stable and reused frequently; add prefill items when small controlled prompts (welcome text, product IDs) appear early in sessions and directly reduce new-token compute."

Sophia (PM): Final note — include a small feedback capture checkbox in post-activation survey: two quick toggles (latency OK / quality OK) + free text. If either toggled No, flag as renewal_risk=true in our CRM.

Anna (CS): Perfect. I'll assemble this into a single doc and send to the onboarding kit. Thanks all :heart: 

Mike (SRE): Added the PromQL to the shared runbooks page. Will ping if we need a follow-up runbook for heavy-throughput customers.
